Garnet v0.8.4 is a research-grade (v0.x) release, not production or 1.0. The full record is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://garnet-lang.org/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell: `irm https://garnet-lang.org/install.ps1 | iex`.

When `gpg` is installed, both installers check that `SHA256SUMS` is signed by the release key they pin for v0.8.4, and stop if it is not. Without `gpg` they warn and check integrity only.

## What changed since v0.8.3

- **Uncatchable enforcement traps (`C1 / BE-F1`).** Capability and depth traps are separated from rescuable user exceptions across the interpreter and VM fallback: `rescue` re-propagates enforcement traps unconditionally, and `ensure { return / break / continue / raise }` cannot mask a trap raised in `try`, `rescue`, or `ensure`.
- **Exhaustive static checker coverage (`FE-F2b`, `FE-F4`).** Safe-mode `try`/`rescue` validation and `CapsGraph` capability propagation now cover `match` guards, `Pattern::Literal`, closures, `BinOp::Pipeline` (`1 |> memory::working`), and arbitrarily nested string interpolations via an O(1)-stack iterative worklist.
- **Release pipeline hardening.** `.github/workflows/vscode-extension.yml` `release-vsix` now runs inside `environment: release`, closing the v0.8.3 gap where VSIX assets could publish before maintainer approval of the `release` environment.
- **Security maintenance.** Resolved `RUSTSEC-2026-0459` (`rusqlite` / SQLite), `RUSTSEC-2026-0543` (removed unmaintained `chrono` transitive dependency), and `RUSTSEC-2026-0592` (`url 2.5.9` / `form_urlencoded 1.2.3`) across workspace and Studio lockfiles under the exact Rust `1.95.0` MSRV floor.
- **Reproducible Paper VI benchmarks & refreshed truth.** Committed deterministic, provider-free harnesses for Paper VI Experiments 2, 4, 5, 6, and 7 (`benchmarks/paper_vi_exp*/`), rematerialized the playground WASM bundle and browser proof, and refreshed `docs/truth.json` (`2,483` passing workspace tests).

## Verify

`SHA256SUMS` is signed with the release key `7431 F1BF AC2A 395D E897  5A3C 3DB8 CC71 3A6B CD50`, listed in [docs/release-signing.md](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/docs/release-signing.md), which also gives the commands. The keys are in [docs/garnet-release-keys.asc](https://github.com/Island-Dev-Crew/garnet/blob/main/docs/garnet-release-keys.asc):

```sh
gpg --import garnet-release-keys.asc
gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
```

## Limits

- Only `@caps` and `@max_depth` trap at run time. `@bounded` step budgets, memory and time ceilings, `@mailbox`, and OS-sandbox application on macOS and Windows are declared, not enforced; seccomp is applied on Linux only.
- The Rust and Go converter frontends drop binary operators, so their output parses but does not compute the same thing.
- WV-6 (native-Windows acceptance) is a disclosed partial.
- The binaries are not code-signed. Garnet Studio is not a release asset.
